Data notes for this edition
  • A clean scan. The collector finished at 07:43 ET Tuesday and every symbol ends on Monday Nov 2's completed bar on every frame; no pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched. The weekly column is the running Nov 2–6 bar, one session old, and its badges are provisional until Friday.
  • Deltas are one session. The prior scan is Monday morning's, which held Friday Oct 30's close, so the change chips, the breadth tile and the census all measure Monday's session.
  • Weekday names. "Monday" in a card is Nov 2, "Friday" Oct 30, "Thursday" Oct 29 and "Wednesday" Oct 28; today's session is "today" or "the open". Hours are named by the time they open: "the first hour" is 09:30–10:30, "the 10:30 hour" the second, "the last hour" 15:30–16:00. The clocks changed on Sunday and every time in this report is Eastern standard time.
  • The weekly column is provisional. On the one-session running bar TSLA turned up from mixed, IGV came off up to mixed, and GOOGL, INTC and HOOD turned down from mixed; SPY's running close sits 2.20 under its 754.30 weekly EMA21 after 30 completed weeks over it, and only Friday's close decides whether the run ends.
  • Two prints are not in the scan. AAPL and PLTR reported after Monday's close; their cards are written on Monday's pre-print bar and open on gap rules, and the feed's direction on both is the only post-print information in this report. AMD reports after today's close, IONQ Thursday, CRWV Tue Nov 10.
  • Volume. The median print was 1.30× the 20-day average; MRVL 2.67×, INTC 1.98×, ORCL 1.85×, XLK 1.66×, PLTR 1.61×, AAPL 1.60× and MSFT 1.58× led, and CRWV's 0.80×, META's 0.84×, SPCX's 0.87× and AVGO's 0.91× were the lightest. 15-minute volume figures are not used.
  • Eight cards carry a daily chart: AAPL, PLTR, AMD, TSLA, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN and MU. Four stances changed on the cards' own rules: AAPL to neutral (under its 21-day into the print), MSFT to cautious (under its 50-day), MU and ORCL to avoid (under their Oct 20 and Oct 28 lows).
  • Firsts and lows, checked against the bars with the averages recomputed from them: SPY's 752.10 is the lowest close since Jul 31; QQQ's since Jul 29 and under its 200-day; SMH's since Jul 29 and under its 200-day; XLK's since Jul 29; IGV's since Sep 11; NVDA's since Jul 31, a second close under its 200-day; MSFT's since Sep 24 and the first under its 50-day since Jul 29; AAPL's since Oct 9 and the first under its 21-day since Oct 1; AMD's since Sep 3; MRVL's since Jul 29 and under its 200-day; ORCL's since Jul 29; INTC's since Apr 8; PLTR's since Sep 18; HOOD's since Jun 9; IONQ's since Apr 9; SNDK's since Jul 29; MU's since Aug 3; META's since Sep 2; GOOGL's since Mar 30; CRWV's 49.46 low is a new 52-week low and its close the lowest since May 1.
  • Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents. NVDA's last hourly close reads 202.20 against a 202.06 daily close, SPY's 752.12 against 752.10, AMD's 466.74 against 466.84; closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars.
  • The daily screenshots show price and volume from the layout; every EMA, RSI, MACD and extension figure in a caption is computed from the scan, not read off the image. The images carry the platform's pre-market quote label; no figure in this report comes from it, and the AAPL and PLTR images end on Monday's pre-print bar.
  • Thin histories: SKHY (no EMA200, no weekly badge), SPCX (no daily EMA200, no weekly badge), CRWV (no weekly EMA200). SKHY's and SPCX's EMA50 are the scan's values on their short histories.
  • The scorecard grades the eight Nov 2 calls on Monday's hourly bars: the AMD and MU shorts worked; the PLTR, MSFT, NVDA and GOOGL longs, each bought at a first-hour close over its reclaim, failed; AAPL's first hour broke its hold and TSLA opened over its first target, so neither triggered. MSFT's secondary short worked from the 14:30 hour.

Bottom line

  • Monday's gap up was sold: 20 of 25 names opened higher, 20 printed the day's high in the first hour and 22 closed in the bottom 15% of their range, an average 3.4% fall.
  • The chips led down into AMD's print: MRVL lost 12.7% on the Lumentum deal news, INTC and ORCL 8.8%, CRWV 8.6%, AMD 7.5%, SNDK 6.6% and MU 5.8%; SMH and QQQ closed under their 200-days.
  • Four stances moved on the cards' own rules: MSFT to cautious under its 50-day, MU and ORCL to avoid, AAPL to neutral into its print; TSLA is the one chart left above its 21-day.
  • AAPL and PLTR reported after the close and the feed has both lower, direction only; AMD reports tonight with the midterms, IONQ Thursday. SPY's running weekly bar sits under its 21-week average.
  • Two of Monday's eight calls paid, the AMD and MU shorts; the four longs bought at a first-hour close over their reclaims failed and two never triggered. Fear & Greed reads 19, extreme fear.

Scorecard: the Nov 2 calls against Monday's bars (2 worked, 4 failed, 2 not triggered)

The first-hour reclaims were traps and the second-hour breaks paid. Monday's eight were written on Friday's 25-of-25 down close and 20 of 25 names gapped up. Four cards opened over or just under their reclaim and the first hour closed over it, so four longs were on from 10:30: PLTR, MSFT, NVDA and GOOGL. None printed a target after the entry hour that was not already printed inside it, every one closed more than half an ATR against the entry, and PLTR and MSFT printed their stops. The two shorts were on from the second hour: AMD closed under 492.21 at 10:30 and printed 475.4 by 13:30, MU closed under 881.52 at 10:30 and printed all three targets. MSFT's secondary short was on from the 14:30 hour and printed 509.40 in the last hour, 4.30 in favour.

Full read: Monday's session, where it leaves the board, and what today decides

Monday was Friday's bounce, sold. Twenty of 25 names opened higher, the first hour printed the high of the day in 20, and 22 printed the low in the last hour and closed in the bottom 15% of their range. The chips carried it: MRVL lost 12.7% on the day it announced a combination with Lumentum, INTC and ORCL 8.8%, CRWV 8.6% to a new 52-week low, AMD 7.5% into tonight's report, SNDK 6.6% and MU 5.8% through its Oct 20 low. The index lost 0.5% to 752.10 at 4% of its range, its lowest close since Jul 31, and its running weekly bar sits under the 21-week average.

Where it leaves the board. The daily column reads 1 up, 4 mixed and 20 down; the 1H column has no up cell and 23 down. One name closes above its 21-day (TSLA), from two; two above the 50-day (TSLA, AAPL), from three; nine of 23 above the 200-day, from twelve, with QQQ, SMH and MRVL dropping out. Fourteen daily charts sit more than two ATR under their mean, from eleven, and INTC at −4.56, GOOGL at −4.21, MRVL at −3.37 and SNDK at −3.00 are past three. Two daily histograms are still positive, TSLA's and SKHY's; ORCL's and AVGO's crossed negative.

What today decides. AAPL and PLTR open on their prints, both lower on the feed, and the cards hold 335.82–334.37 and 178.13–177.64 or they do not: a close under 334.37 turns AAPL cautious, a close under 171.87 turns PLTR avoid. AMD is a day trade until the bell and an event bet after it. The index questions are whether SPY closes back over 754.30 and QQQ over 684.94, and whether NVDA takes back 205.46 and MSFT 509.31 before the two Wednesday chip prints. Fear & Greed reads 19, extreme fear, from 23 at Monday's close; the feed has the Nasdaq-100 in its third correction of the year, direction only.

Sentiment and sources

Sentiment. CNN Fear & Greed reads 19 ("extreme fear") on this morning's fetch at 07:21 ET, from 23 at Monday's close, 33 a week ago and 38 a month ago on the same fetch. The gauge has fallen through 25 into the extreme band on a session the index lost half a percent, which says more about breadth than about the index: 22 of 25 names on this board fell and 23 are negative on the month. The series drifts between fetches (Monday's fetch read 30 for the week-ago point that today's reads as 33), so the direction is relied on and the level is approximate.

Headline feed (Tuesday morning, direction only): the Nasdaq-100 tumbling into its third correction this year as AI worries mount; Apple's stock falling after its report, with a memory-cost squeeze on profits in the coverage; Palantir lower after its report with bookings growth blamed; hedge funds hit in October's AI rout; Apollo lending a record sum into the AI financing boom; Wall Street's most hated stocks faring better than its favourites; the midterms described as able to jolt stocks and the market said to love gridlock; oil edging back up after sharp declines; Pfizer lifting its full-year outlook; Yum Brands beating with Taco Bell weighing; Goldman naming winners and losers after the Binance theft; ultra-short bond ETFs drawing heavy October inflows. Tuesday trades one hold and a row of floors: TSLA is bought on 400.53–397.71; AAPL and PLTR open on gap rules against 335.82–334.37 and 178.13–177.64; AMD is a day trade off 466.07 until the bell; NVDA, MSFT, MU, AMZN and GOOGL trade Monday's lows as floors with hourly reclaims, and a first-hour close over a reclaim is not bought until the second hour holds it.

Session framing

Monday gapped 20 of 25 names up, printed the high of the day in the first hour in 20, the low in the last hour in 22, and closed 22 in the bottom 15% of their range. Only AMZN and TSLA printed their low in the first hour. Every long the cards had bought at a first-hour close over its reclaim failed (PLTR, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, and HOOD, SPCX, IONQ and AVGO off the calls list); every short on from a second-hour close under its line paid (AMD, MU, MRVL, ORCL, CRWV) or came close (INTC, SNDK). The index closed at 4% of its range, its lowest since Jul 31, and QQQ and SMH closed under their 200-days.

Four questions govern the session. Where do AAPL and PLTR open on their prints, and does the first hour hold 334.37 and 177.64: a close under the first turns AAPL cautious, a close under 171.87 turns PLTR avoid. Does the gap-and-fade repeat: Monday's rule, taken into today, is that a first-hour close over a reclaim is bought only when the 10:30 hour holds the reclaim too. Does AMD hold 466.07 into its print, and do the memory names (MU 829.24, SNDK 1067.40) hold with it. And does SPY close back over 754.30 and QQQ over 684.94, the two averages Monday's close lost. Nothing on the AMD card is held past 16:00.

Methodology and data notes

Pipeline, rubric, data caveats and sources

Pipeline: TradingView Desktop (CDP) → dedicated "B List Research" layout → up to 500 bars per timeframe per symbol (W / D / 240 / 60 / 15, regular sessions) → indicators computed locally: EMA 10/21/50/200, RSI-14 (Wilder), MACD 12/26/9, ATR-14 (Wilder), 20-bar relative volume, fractal (2-2) swing pivots, 252-day high/low distances, relative strength vs SPY as return differentials. Trend matrix rubric per cell, ±1 for each of six inputs: close vs EMA21, close vs EMA50, EMA21/EMA50 stack, EMA50 five-bar slope, RSI zone (≥55 = +1, ≤45 = −1, else 0) and MACD histogram sign — score ≥+4 Up, ≤−4 Down, else Chop; cells lacking an EMA21 or EMA50 return "—".

Data caveats. Captured Tuesday Nov 3 2026 at 07:43 ET, before the open; no errors were reported across the 25 symbols and every symbol ends on Monday Nov 2's completed session on every frame. No pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched. The prior scan for every day-over-day comparison (change chips, breadth tile, census) is Monday morning's, which held Friday Oct 30's completed session, so every delta on this page is exactly one session, Monday's. The weekly column is the running Nov 2–6 bar, one session old, and its badges are provisional until Friday's close; SPY's running close sits under its 21-week average after 30 completed weeks over it, and that claim is recounted each Saturday. "Monday" in the cards is Nov 2, "Friday" Oct 30, "Thursday" Oct 29 and "Wednesday" Oct 28; today's session is "today" or "the open". The clocks changed on Sunday Nov 1 and every time in this report is Eastern standard time; hours are named by the time they open ("the first hour" is 09:30–10:30, "the last hour" 15:30–16:00). The 15m column is Monday's 15:45 ET bar. The final 15m bars carry the usual closing-auction volume spike and those RVOL figures were not used anywhere in this report; 15-minute readings quoted are RSI, extension and EMA position only. The same applies to 1H and 4H relative volume. All relative-volume figures in this report are daily. Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents at the open and the close (auction prints); closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars. Fractal pivot lag. Swing pivots require two bars on each side to confirm, so a level set within the last two bars will not yet appear in the pivot sequence; Wednesday Oct 28's highs have confirmed as pivots across the board and no Thursday, Friday or Monday level is in any list yet. Those sessions' highs and lows are quoted from the bars, not the pivot lists. "Lowest close since", "first close under … since", "N lower closes" and "new 52-week low" claims were checked against the daily bars with the 10-, 21- and 50-day averages recomputed from them; every 200-day figure is the scan's. SKHY's and SPCX's daily EMA50 are the scan's values on their short histories. AAPL and PLTR reported after Monday's close; their post-print bars are not in the scan, their cards are written on Monday's pre-print bar and open on gap rules, and the feed's direction on both is the only post-print information in this report. AMD reports after today's close and IONQ Thursday; their cards are day trades until the print and gap rules after it. Scorecard. The Nov 2 edition's eight flagged calls, written on Friday's close, are graded against Monday's hourly and daily bars: the hourly bars decide "held an hour" and the daily close decides the invalidation. A long is on from the close of the first hour that closes over its reclaim when the open sat under the first target and the hour held the zone (PLTR, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL); a target that prints inside the entry hour, before that hour closes, does not count for the entry (NVDA, SPCX, AVGO off the calls list); a long that prints its stop after the entry, or closes more than a third of an ATR against it with no target, is failed (all four); a first target printed by a point after the entry and then a stop does not rescue the grade (MSFT). A short is on from the close of the first hour that closes under its line, including when the open already sat under the line but above the first target (ORCL off the calls list); an open under the stop and under the first short target sets up neither side. A short that triggers, prints no target and closes more than a third of an ATR in its favour is a partial (INTC, SNDK), within a fifth of an ATR a wash (IONQ). An open over the first target is not an entry (TSLA, SKHY); a first hour that breaks the hold zone before any reclaim is not triggered (AAPL); a line first closed through in the last hour is not triggered, no session left (PLTR's short, META's). A secondary trade on the same card is graded in the note and not in the tally (MSFT's short worked). Stance changes follow each card's own stated rule: AAPL closed under its 21-day (neutral), MSFT under its 50-day (cautious), MU under its Oct 20 low and ORCL under its Oct 28 low (avoid); "held a session" means a second close on the right side of a line, so no upgrade is possible before Wednesday's close.
